clue.text: Missile launch reported in coastal plant

parts.note: SAM is a surface-to-air missile

indicators.note: reported means the word for launching is given as it would be heard, spelt differently

parts.note: to launch a missile is to fire it

explanation.surface: A missile launch is announced somewhere along the coast, among the vegetation.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock samphire is a fleshy edible plant growing on sea cliffs and salt marshes.

clue.text: Lost cities heartlessly demolished, a turning point

indicators.note: demolished means the combined letters are knocked down and rebuilt in a new order
heartlessly says the middle two letters are removed from the cities word

explanation.surface: Ruined cities lost forever mark a moment when history changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartlessly' cuts TI from CITIES, leaving CIES; 'demolished' rearranges LOST and CIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomy: the sun appears to stop and reverse direction at midsummer and midwinter, a turning point of the year.

clue.text: Soft rock publication mostly reproduced

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter of the copy is dropped
reproduced says the publication word appears a second time

parts.note: mag is short for magazine

explanation.surface: A soft rock music magazine, largely copied.
explanation.walkthrough: MAG repeated gives MAGMAG; 'mostly' drops the final G.
explanation.definitionFit: Geology: molten material beneath the earth's crust is rock in a soft, liquid state.

clue.text: Statement of obvious success

parts.note: split three-apostrophe-one-three, the letters state a tautology about temperature, while the whole is a successful person

explanation.surface: Someone is plainly doing well.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase with an apostrophe after the third letter, it says something warm is warm, a statement of the obvious; together it is a star performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal noun: a highly successful, skilled person, often a flashy one.

clue.text: Thoroughly beat flour and butter for variable time

indicators.note: for says the time letter stands in place of the variable letter

parts.note: a roux is flour cooked in butter as a sauce base
X is the classic algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: beat flour and butter well, timing as needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to rout an enemy is to defeat it decisively.

clue.text: Hit in street fight

parts.note: a ruck is a scuffle or brawl

explanation.surface: Someone was punched during a brawl out on the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense synonym: to have struck someone is to have hit them.

clue.text: One of three Mediterranean cities featured on radio three times?

indicators.note: on radio says the word is as heard over the airwaves, spelt another way

parts.note: triply means three times over

explanation.surface: A city mentioned on the wireless three times over.
explanation.walkthrough: Tripoli is in Libya, in Lebanon and in Greece; the sound match is approximate, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Place name shared: the capital of Libya, a Lebanese port, and a Greek town all bear it.

clue.text: Regularly furnish singular 'hair of the dog' for free

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the next word, here the second, fourth and sixth

parts.note: hackles are the hairs on a dog's neck; one of them is a hackle

explanation.surface: Instructions to provide a single hangover drink, free of charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hair of the dog' usually means a morning-after drink, but here it is literal dog hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to unchain or release someone is to set them free.

clue.text: Again look up custodian of the net

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the prefix re- means again
a peek is a quick look

explanation.surface: Check again for whoever looks after the online network.
explanation.definitionFit: Sport: the goalkeeper guards the goal net in football or hockey.

clue.text: What'll brighten up the room — pale daffodil, perhaps

parts.note: a pale colour is a light one
a daffodil grows from a bulb, so it is an example of one

explanation.surface: A pale yellow daffodil cheers up a room, says the interior decorator.
explanation.definitionFit: Descriptive definition: an electric lamp is the thing that makes a dark room bright.

clue.text: Hide money with family

parts.note: bucks are dollars
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Conceal cash with relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun sense: leather made from deer skin is an animal hide.

clue.text: Kids matter

definitions.meaning: offspring, as in dying without children
a topic or point under discussion

explanation.surface: Children are important, a slogan might say.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: one's offspring in legal language, and a subject or problem being debated.

clue.text: Poor quality wood used in test

indicators.note: used in says the tree's word is placed within the word for test

parts.note: to try something is to test it
ash is a timber tree

explanation.surface: Cheap timber was used in a trial, implying shoddy work.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something cheap and tawdry is of low quality.

clue.text: Praise from a spymaster upon cypher being broken by secondary characters in Bletchley Park

indicators.note: upon says the opening letters sit ahead of what follows in the across entry

parts.note: C is the code letter traditionally used for the head of MI6, Britain's foreign intelligence service

indicators.note: being broken by says the cypher word is split open by other letters

parts.note: a code is a cypher

indicators.note: secondary characters means the second letter of each of the two following words

explanation.surface: A spy chief's commendation after a code was cracked by back-room staff at Bletchley Park.
explanation.walkthrough: Bletchley Park was Britain's wartime codebreaking centre. 'Secondary characters in' gives L and A, which break CODE into COLADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an accolade is an award or expression of high praise.

clue.text: Man's fear of Latin?

parts.note: his is the possessive for a man
panic is sudden fear

explanation.surface: A man's dread of studying the Latin language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin' suggests the old language; here it means Latin American.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective sense: of Spanish-speaking or Latin American origin.

clue.text: Bird pursues mite that's found in cherry?

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
to tail someone is to follow them
a tick is a small parasitic mite-like arachnid

explanation.surface: A bird chases a tiny creature living in a cherry.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a cherry in a drink is often speared on a small pointed wooden pick.

clue.text: Flower display in emo club

indicators.note: display means the letters are set out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A flower arrangement at a club for emo music fans.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: aquilegia, a garden flower with spurred petals, has this common name.

clue.text: Noisy, mean chap

parts.note: to mean to do something is to plan it
a gent is a gentleman, a chap

explanation.surface: A loud, stingy fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like stingy, but it is the verb intend.
explanation.definitionFit: Near synonym: a resonant, mournful sound is loud and reverberating.

clue.text: Corrupt old earl's hanging round outside toilet for minister

indicators.note: hanging round outside says the rearranged letters surround the word for toilet
corrupt means the letters of the words that follow are rearranged

parts.note: a privy is an outdoor toilet

explanation.surface: A dishonest aristocrat loiters near a lavatory, scandal for a government figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Title: this is a senior British cabinet office, holder of the monarch's personal seal.

clue.text: Entourage always holding one up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the combined letters are read bottom to top
holding says the poetic word contains the number word

parts.note: e'er is a poetic contraction of ever
a unit is the number one

explanation.surface: A celebrity's followers keep someone propped up at all times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding' makes a container, and 'up' reverses the result, which works because this is a down entry. E'er is poetic shorthand for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a group of attendants accompanying an important person.

clue.text: Saying 'Why, oh… Britain these days!' is a conversational filler

indicators.note: saying means the exclamation is rendered as the letters it is heard as

parts.note: the exclamation as spoken, two words pronounced like two letters
UK is the United Kingdom
now means at present

explanation.surface: A grumble in the 'Why, oh why' style about modern Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a stock phrase people insert into speech while thinking, with little meaning.

clue.text: Remains in talked-about underworld location

indicators.note: talked-about means the river name as heard, spelt differently

parts.note: the Styx is the river of the Greek underworld

explanation.surface: Human remains found in a much-discussed hellish place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' looks like a noun (bodies) but is the verb stays.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: something that stays fixed in place persists.

clue.text: Short-term employment around Thailand's capital is attractive

indicators.note: around says the temp-work word goes round the letter picked

parts.note: temping is working in temporary jobs

indicators.note: capital means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Taking temporary work in Bangkok sounds appealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something enticing or alluring tempts you.

clue.text: Call big meeting on replacing it

indicators.note: replacing says one word takes the place of another within the meeting word

parts.note: a summit is a meeting of leaders
taken as written

explanation.surface: Convene a major conference in place of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to summon someone is to call them to come.

clue.text: Coded instruction from a crossword's setting

indicators.note: setting means the letters are embedded in the following words, like a stone in a mount

explanation.surface: A cryptic instruction found in a puzzle's construction.
explanation.definitionFit: Computing: a single command that expands into a set of programmed instructions.

clue.text: Main part of foot

definitions.meaning: chief or principal, as in a chief rival
the curved underside between heel and toes

explanation.surface: The principal section of the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: an adjective for chief, and the bony curve of the sole.

clue.text: Dog that'll guide one in mountains?

definitions.meaning: a ... terrier, a small Scottish breed
a pile of stones set up as a landmark on a hill or trail

explanation.surface: A guide dog for walkers lost on the peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a small Scottish terrier breed, and a heap of stones marking a mountain route.

clue.text: Abysmal article in French paper

parts.note: chronic is informal British for very bad
le is the French definite article

explanation.surface: A dreadful piece in a French newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspaper name: many papers are called the Chronicle, so it stands for a newspaper.

clue.text: What you do when sailing past Gib became apparent

parts.note: what you do on passing a sight is see it
sailing east past Gibraltar brings the Mediterranean, the Med, into view

explanation.surface: A traveller notes what happens on a cruise past the Rock of Gibraltar.
explanation.walkthrough: Gib is short for Gibraltar, at the western mouth of the Mediterranean: ships heading east past it have that sea ahead of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to appear or come across a certain way; strictly 'appeared' rather than 'became apparent'.

clue.text: Cast who boast are theatrically ostentatious

indicators.note: cast as in throwing the letters, so the words that follow are rearranged

explanation.surface: Actors who brag are flamboyant on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to show off flamboyantly, like performers on the old river theatre boats.
